note: agent-guard runs this CLI to distribute an already-scanned skill into every agent on the machine, and in project mode to stage a pinned commit (owner/repo#sha) into a throw-away directory before the scan. GuardDog returns BLOCK on the same four findings as for 1.7.0; the two GitHub token reads only moved from dist/cli.mjs into the bundled chunk dist/_chunks/remove.mjs (getGitHubToken). Each finding is accepted with a reason AND neutralised by how the wrapper invokes the CLI (npm_config_ignore_scripts=true, reduced environment without token variables). Raised from 1.7.0 for the fixes in 1.7.5 (VULN-16995: skill symlinks are no longer dereferenced outside the skill directory), 1.7.6 and 1.9.0 (symlinks confined), and 1.8.0 (install and remove no longer delete agent category directories or unmanaged files). New in 1.9.0 and not a GuardDog finding: when an unauthenticated GitHub API request is rate-limited or answered 401/404, the CLI retries the same GET through `gh api` (fetchGitHubApiWithGitHubCli), so an existing GitHub CLI login on the machine is used for that request. The request goes only to the GitHub host and reads the repository tree agent-guard asked for; the token stays inside gh. This is the same class as the git clone fallback 1.7.0 already had, which uses the machine's git credential helper. Any other finding, in this or a later version, stops delegation and the built-in installer takes over.

findings.reason: husky is the package's own git-hook tooling for development. npm runs `prepare` only on publish/pack, on an argument-less local `npm install`, on `npm install <folder>` and for git dependencies -- never for a registry tarball and not under npx. The wrapper additionally sets npm_config_ignore_scripts=true, so no lifecycle script can run at all.
Agent detection: the presence of COPILOT_* variables identifies a GitHub Copilot session. The value is used as a signal, and the variable is not present in the reduced environment the wrapper passes.
Same private-repository code path as GITHUB_TOKEN (getGitHubToken), reading the GitHub CLI's variable. Not present in the reduced environment the wrapper passes.

Documented feature: getGitHubToken reads a GitHub token, which fetchGitHubApi sends only as the Authorization header of GitHub API requests, to reach private repositories; the other use only checks whether a token is set to print a hint. agent-guard stages public repositories, and the delegated process runs with a reduced environment that contains no token variables.
